input: Get a structural engineer to inspect the basement crack

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The nature and size of the crack determines urgency and what kind of inspection is needed — a hairline shrinkage crack is very different from a horizontal or stair-step crack that could signal foundation failure.
The property type (owned home, rental, commercial building) and location affects which engineers are available, whether landlord or HOA is responsible, and local licensing requirements.
Knowing whether the user already has a contractor, home inspector, or engineer in mind — or needs to find one from scratch — changes the first action entirely.
Budget for the inspection and any potential repairs affects which engineer tier to target (independent specialist vs. large firm) and whether insurance or a home warranty might cover the cost.
How quickly the inspection needs to happen determines whether this is an urgent same-week booking or a scheduled appointment, and influences which outreach channels to prioritize.
The user may just want a verbal assessment, or they may need a formal written report for insurance, a home sale, or a mortgage lender — this changes what to ask the engineer to deliver.
The user may prefer a specific way to find the engineer — personal referral, online search, their insurance company, or a home warranty service — which shapes the recommended approach.

gold.taskTitle: Get a structural engineer to inspect basement crack
gold.taskDescription: Find and hire a structural engineer to professionally inspect a crack in the basement and assess whether it poses a structural risk.

questions.title: What does the crack look like and how large is it?
questions.description: Understanding the crack's appearance (hairline, horizontal, stair-step, wide) and size helps determine urgency and the scope of inspection required.

questions.title: Is this your own home, a rental, or another property type?
questions.description: Property ownership and type affects who is responsible for hiring the engineer and which local licensing rules apply.

questions.title: Do you already have an engineer or contractor in mind?
questions.description: Knowing whether the user has an existing contact or needs to find one from scratch determines the very first action to take.

questions.title: What is your budget for the inspection itself?
questions.description: Budget constrains which engineers or firms to target and whether insurance, a home warranty, or out-of-pocket payment is the route.

questions.title: How soon do you need the inspection to happen?
questions.description: Urgency determines whether to pursue emergency same-week availability or a standard scheduled appointment.

questions.title: Do you need a formal written report as an outcome?
questions.description: Some situations (home sale, insurance claim, mortgage) require a stamped written report, while others only need a verbal professional opinion.

questions.title: How do you prefer to find and vet the engineer?
questions.description: The user may prefer a personal referral, an online directory, their insurance company, or a home warranty service — this shapes the recommended search approach.
